standard.title: Analyse target language texts using metalanguage
standard.description: analyse a range of target language texts, using metalanguage to explain linguistic, textual and cultural elements
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can reflect on and explain similarities and differences between target language and English, support younger learners, and analyse metaphorical meaning (AC9LCH8U03). They have applied comparative metalanguage across text types. They have not yet analysed stylistic devices in target language texts, compared genre organisation across languages, described genres unique to target language literary tradition, or used metalanguage to explain linguistic, textual and cultural elements simultaneously.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse a range of target language texts using metalanguage to explain linguistic, textual and cultural elements — including stylistic devices, genre conventions, structural analysis, and culturally-specific literary forms.

nodes.label: Stylistic devices and rhetorical analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and analyse stylistic devices used in target language texts — including rhetorical, figurative and structural devices — and evaluate their effectiveness.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three stylistic devices in a target language text, explain how each works using metalanguage, and evaluate the effectiveness of at least one.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse stylistic devices in target language written texts — parallel structures, double negatives, figurative devices, rhetorical questions; use metalanguage to explain their function; evaluate the effectiveness of specific devices; compare stylistic conventions in target language and English texts.
wider: Produce a full stylistic analysis of a target language text — annotating every stylistic device with metalanguage and evaluating how each contributes to the text's overall effect
Compare how the same rhetorical effect is achieved differently in target language and English texts — identify genre-specific and culturally-specific stylistic conventions
nodes.hinge_reason: Stylistic device analysis is the prerequisite for full text analysis at Y9-10. Students who cannot identify and name stylistic devices cannot produce the linguistic, textual and cultural analysis that this descriptor requires — nor can they apply these insights to their own text creation.

response_modes.reason: Stylistic device analysis requires students to identify a device, name it using metalanguage, explain its function, and evaluate its effectiveness — a multi-step analytical process. Explicit stylistic analysis instruction with varied model texts builds this systematic capacity before students can analyse independently.

success_criteria: Identifies at least three stylistic devices in a target language text using metalanguage
Evaluates the effectiveness of at least one device with explanation

nodes.label: Genre organisation and content development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how content is structured and ideas are developed in different target language genres, including how genre conventions compare across languages.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse the structural organisation of at least two different target language text types, explaining how ideas are ordered and developed in each, and comparing with English conventions for at least one.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how text types structure content and develop ideas; compare how information is exchanged using culturally-accepted patterns; compare essay-writing conventions — position placement, argument structure — across languages; analyse linguistic features for different text purposes; categorise cultural and linguistic elements.
wider: Compare essay organisation conventions in the target language with English — explain where the author's position appears, how evidence is marshalled, and what this reveals about cultural epistemological conventions
Apply understanding of genre organisation to produce a text that authentically follows target language conventions — then compare with what the same text would look like following English conventions

response_modes.reason: Genre organisation analysis must be applied across varied text types — analytical essay, news article, literary prose, formal report — before students can generalise their analytical capacity. Single-genre analysis produces genre-specific rather than transferable text analysis skills.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding how genre organisation differs across languages — particularly how target language essay and argument conventions differ from English — is a genuinely valuable academic insight that background learners can leverage in both languages. Width investment here develops bilingual academic literacy.
success_criteria: Analyses the structural organisation of at least two different target language text types
Compares organisational conventions with English for at least one text type

nodes.label: Culturally-specific literary genres and traditions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the purpose and features of genres unique to target language literary tradition, exploring their origins and demonstrating cultural knowledge in text analysis.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one genre unique to the target language literary tradition, describe its key features using metalanguage, and explain its cultural origins or significance.
nodes.typical_width: Describe and analyse genres unique to target language literary tradition; explore their origins in traditional literature; explain cultural purposes and conventions; compare with equivalent or non-equivalent forms in English literary tradition; apply cultural knowledge in text analysis.
wider: Produce a text in a target language literary genre — apply genre conventions authentically and reflect on what cultural knowledge was required to do so
Research the historical development of a target language literary genre — trace how it has evolved from traditional to contemporary forms and what has changed

response_modes.reason: Culturally-specific genre analysis integrates stylistic device knowledge (node 1) and genre organisation understanding (node 2) into a full cultural-literary analysis. The teaching investment is in creating genuine engagement with target language literary tradition — students as culturally-informed readers, not only linguistic analysts.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one genre unique to the target language literary tradition with key features described using metalanguage
Explains the cultural origins or significance of the genre
